What this pack covers

One pack for Standard Level IB Chemistry: theory lessons with interactive simulations, a glossary, and exam-style practice in the format of Paper 1A, 1B and 2. Units follow a common two-year scheme of work (the ibchem possible scheme). This sample includes Units 1 and 2. The remaining units would follow the same format. Content marked Additional higher level in the IB guide is left out.

SubtopicUnitLessonsPractice questionsGuide timePack study time (est.)

Structure 1.4 The mole14 to 9Yes7 h

Guide time is the recommended teaching time at SL, including teacher-led class time. Pack study time is our estimate for reading the lessons and answering their checks. It does not include practicals, graded practice or practice papers. Your school's scheme of work may differ.

Practice marks in this pack

Daily 5

Five short questions a day, chosen from the lessons you have started. Questions you get right come back after longer gaps. Questions you miss come back sooner.

How Daily 5 works
  • Each question sits in a box from 1 to 5. A right answer moves it up one box. A wrong answer sends it back to Box 1.
  • The gaps before a question returns are 1, 2, 4, 7 and 14 days for Boxes 1 to 5. These gaps are a simple scheme chosen for this pack, not tuned to any one learner.
  • A question you miss is asked once more at the end of the session. That second try does not change its box.
  • A day counts towards your streak when you finish a Daily 5 session.
  • Check questions answered in a lesson and Paper 1A answers also feed the boxes.
  • Everything is saved in this browser only.

Data booklet map for Unit 1

Students must have a clean copy of the IB Chemistry data booklet in the course and in exams. This map tells you where to look. Use the official booklet from your school or the IB, not an unofficial copy.

You needOpen booklet sectionUsed in lessons
Relative atomic masses (2 d.p.)Section 7, The periodic table5, 6, 7, 8, 15 to 18, 20
n = m / M and n = CVSection 1, Some relevant equations6, 8, 15
PV = nRT and P1V1/T1 = P2V2/T2Section 1, Some relevant equations13
Percentage atom economySection 1, Some relevant equations18
Avogadro constant, gas constant, molar volume at STPSection 2, Physical constants4, 12, 13
SI prefixes (such as milli, centi)Section 3, Metric (SI) multipliers8, 13
Kelvin conversion, dm3 to m3, STP and SATPSection 4, Unit conversions and standard conditions3, 12, 13
Uncertainty propagation (for practical work)Section 23, UncertaintiesPractical work

Values used in this pack (from booklet sections 2 and 4)

ItemValue
Avogadro constant, NA6.02 × 1023 mol-1
Gas constant, R8.31 J K-1 mol-1
Molar volume of an ideal gas at STP2.27 × 10-2 m3 mol-1 = 22.7 dm3 mol-1
STP273.15 K and 100 kPa
SATP298.15 K and 100 kPa
Temperature conversionT (K) = θ (°C) + 273.15
Volume conversion1 dm3 = 1 litre = 1 × 10-3 m3 = 1 × 103 cm3
The booklet lists STP as 273.15 K and 100 kPa. Older materials often use 273 K and 101.3 kPa, which gives a different molar volume. Make sure students use the booklet values.

Command terms used in this pack

IB questions are worded around command terms. These definitions are from the IB Chemistry guide glossary.

TermWhat to do
Compare and contrastDescribe the differences between two or more items or situations, addressing each one throughout.
DeduceReach a conclusion from the information given.
DetermineObtain the only possible answer.
DiscussGive a balanced, considered review covering a range of arguments, factors or hypotheses, with conclusions supported by evidence.
EvaluateAppraise something by weighing its strengths and limitations.
ExplainGive a detailed account that includes reasons or causes.
PredictState an expected result.
SketchRepresent something with a labelled diagram or graph showing the general shape or relationship and relevant features.
SuggestPropose a solution, hypothesis or other possible answer.
Other terms (such as State, Calculate, Describe, Outline) appear in the questions. Add their official definitions from the IB glossary before publishing the full version.

Relationships and constants used

ItemValue or relationship
Amount, mass, molar massn = m / M
Amount, concentration, volumen = c V (c in mol dm-3, V in dm3)
Ideal gas equationPV = nRT (SI units: Pa, m3, K)
Combined gas lawP1V1 / T1 = P2V2 / T2
Avogadro constant6.02 × 1023 mol-1
Gas constant R8.31 J K-1 mol-1
TemperatureT (K) = θ (°C) + 273.15
Unit conversions1 dm3 = 1000 cm3 = 10-3 m3; 1 cm3 = 10-6 m3; 1 kPa = 1000 Pa
The guide says the relationships above are in the IB data booklet. Check the constants against the current official booklet. Relative atomic masses used in this pack: H 1.01, C 12.01, O 16.00, Na 22.99, Cl 35.45, Ca 40.08.
